name: check-the-maps
description: A fast, low-cost pre-flight check for Copilot prompts. Clear prompts go straight through; vague ones get quick questions and a suggested rewrite, using MAPS (Mission, Ask, Parameters, Shape).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, the workspace can't choose the framework, the checker model or the chat mode. Your user settings are used instead.

chatParticipants.name: maps
chatParticipants.description: Your prompt is checked, then sent to Copilot

commands.name: check
commands.description: Check a prompt without sending it

commands.name: send
commands.description: Skip the check and send straight to Copilot

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the active prompt framework (MAPS by default)

checkTheMaps.autoSend.markdownDescription: Send prompts that pass the check to Copilot automatically. When off, a passing prompt shows a **Send to Copilot** button instead.

enumDescriptions: Mission, Ask, Parameters, Shape. The default.
Context, Objective, Style, Tone, Audience, Response. From GovTech Singapore's Data Science & AI team. Style and Tone are optional for coding prompts.
Role, Instructions, Steps, End goal, Narrowing. Role and Steps are optional for coding prompts.
Role, Task, Format. The lightest checklist. Role is optional for coding prompts.
Your own checklist, defined in Check The MAPS: Custom Framework.
checkTheMaps.framework.markdownDescription: The checklist prompts are checked against. Each framework says which of its parts each request size needs, so small edits stay quick. Set this in your workspace settings to share a choice with your team. [Choose Prompt Framework](command:checkTheMaps.chooseFramework) compares them.

enumDescriptions: Only flag prompts that are likely to go wrong. Fewest interruptions.
Flag prompts that leave out something important for their size.
Flag any prompt that skips a part its size needs. Good for learning a framework.
checkTheMaps.strictness.markdownDescription: How picky the check is. Small, specific requests (like renaming a function) always pass.

checkTheMaps.customFramework.markdownDescription: Your own framework, used when **Framework** is set to `custom`. List its parts in `elements`, name the part that states the task itself in `taskElement`, and say which parts each request size needs in `requiredBySize` (sizes: `small`, `task`, `large`, `design`). Missing pieces get sensible defaults. [Choose Prompt Framework](command:checkTheMaps.chooseFramework) can create a starter framework for you.

name.description: Short name shown in messages, such as "Our checklist".

anyOf.description: A part, given by its label alone.

id.description: Short id used internally, such as "context". Defaults to the label in lowercase.

meaning.description: What this part means, as a phrase, such as "files, constraints and what must not change".

example.description: An optional short example, shown in /explain.

elements.description: The parts of the checklist, in order.

taskElement.description: The id of the part that states the task itself. Small requests need only this part.

requiredBySize.description: Which parts each request size needs, by id.

small.description: Small, specific edits and questions. Only the task part is checked.

task.description: Bug fixes and features in existing code.

checkTheMaps.model.markdownDescription: The id of the model that checks your prompts. Leave empty to use the cheapest model with a known price; a premium model is never picked automatically. [Choose Checker Model](command:checkTheMaps.chooseModel) shows every available model with its cost per check.

checkTheMaps.keepMapsInChatBox.markdownDescription: After a prompt is sent to Copilot, put `@maps` back in the Chat view's chat box so your next prompt is checked too. Delete it to send a prompt without a check.

checkTheMaps.sendInMode.markdownDescription: Chat mode to send passing prompts in, such as `agent` or `ask`, or the name of a custom agent. Leave empty to keep whatever mode the chat is in. Note that switching into or out of `edit` mode can start a new chat session.

checkTheMaps.timeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds to wait for the checker before sending the prompt on unchecked. Checks usually take one to two seconds.

checkTheMaps.dailyCheckLimit.markdownDescription: Most model checks per day. After that, prompts are sent on unchecked. Prompts that pass the local rules don't count. Set to `0` for no limit.

checkTheMaps.showStatusBar.markdownDescription: Show the MAPS item in the status bar, with a green check after a passing prompt.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Check The MAPS
walkthroughs.description: Catch vague prompts before they cost you a round of rework.

steps.title: Check your first prompt
steps.description:
Start a chat prompt with @maps. Clear prompts go straight to Copilot with a small ✅. Vague ones get a few quick questions and a suggested rewrite.
[Start a Checked Prompt](command:checkTheMaps.startCheckedPrompt)

steps.title: Pick your prompt framework (optional)
steps.description:
Prompts are checked against MAPS (Dan Martell) by default. You can switch to CO-STAR, RISEN or RTF, or define your own checklist for your team.
[Choose Prompt Framework](command:checkTheMaps.chooseFramework)

steps.title: Pick the checker model (optional)
steps.description:
By default, the cheapest model with a known price checks your prompts, at a tiny fraction of a credit per check. You can choose a different one.
[Choose Checker Model](command:checkTheMaps.chooseModel)

steps.title: Tune how strict it is
steps.description:
Lenient is the default and interrupts least. Strict is good while you're learning MAPS.
[Set Strictness](command:checkTheMaps.setStrictness)

steps.title: Let Copilot check too (optional)
steps.description:
Add a short section to your repository's Copilot instructions, so Copilot itself asks before guessing on big requests and keeps answers in scope, even for prompts you send without @maps.
[Add Guidance to Copilot Instructions](command:checkTheMaps.addInstructions)

steps.title: Learn your framework
steps.description:
What each part of your framework means, and which requests need it.
[Explain the Prompt Framework](command:checkTheMaps.explain)
